raw_response:
I've been farming these fields in Quzhou County my whole life — over forty years now, since I was a boy helping my father. I never went to school, but I know this land and this climate better than any book ever could. Everyone in our village grows the same two crops: winter wheat and summer maize. That's what the North China Plain is made for. I have about 8 mu of good flat land, and I double-crop it — wheat from October to June, then maize planted right after the wheat harvest until September. I don't bother with cotton anymore; I'm getting older and my back can't handle all those sprayings, and the wheat-maize rotation gives me steady grain I can sell to the local buyers without worry. For wheat, I'll rotary till the soil after the maize stalks are cleared, sow my improved Jimai seeds, put down basal compound fertilizer and topdress with urea at green-up, irrigate three times (before winter, at jointing, and at heading), and spray for weeds and diseases maybe three times. For maize, there's no time to waste after the wheat comes out in early June — I direct-seed hybrid Denghai605 with no-tillage to catch the season, apply fertilizer, irrigate once or twice if the rains fail, and spray for weeds and borers a couple of times. That's the way it's always been done, and that's the way I'll do it again this year.
